notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Private for on-prem, air-gapped contact center automation (gov/defense use). Primary ask = agent assist + ticket summarization + real-time tool-calling into on-prem ITSM. High-level constraints: IL5-like controls, no outbound internet from inference hosts, HSM-backed keys, long retention/immutable audit logs.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-02-15: Intro demo (Priya + Ethan) — showed hosted vs private options; Aegis liked stream/fallback idea. Fireflies id ff_2026-02-15_ARS-demo.
- 2026-02-25: Security intake call with Aegis SecOps (Lena present). They sent security questionnaire; flagged FIPS/HSM and air-gap requirements.
- 2026-03-02: First technical deep-dive with infra team. Discussed network architecture: isolated VLANs, no direct upstream to Redwood control plane unless customer-managed control plane in DMZ.
- 2026-03-08: POC scoping call — target: deploy Private control plane in Aegis lab, run performance test with 1,000 concurrent agents and 200ms avg response SLO for agent-assist microcalls.
- 2026-03-09: Security follow-up — Aegis provided sample HSM vendor docs and requested KMS/HSM integration playbook. Jira tickets opened JIRA-CC-1123 (connectivity) + JIRA-Security-541 (HSM questions).

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria (customer language / paraphrased):
- "Must run air-gapped; inference compute cannot phone home. Control plane can be customer-hosted in DMZ with signed artifacts."
- On-prem deployment with per-model pinning and deterministic rollbacks.
- Latency SLO: 150-250ms token generation for short-turn dialogs; 200ms average desired for assist calls.
- Burst tolerance: sustain 1,000 concurrent agent sessions, spikes up to 2,500 for 10-15 minutes.
- Tool-calling: integrate with ServiceNow instance (on-prem) via an outbound-only connector; support for idempotent retries and circuit-breakers.
- Audit & retention: immutable audit logs for 7 years, token-level cost breakdowns are nice-to-have but must be derivable from offline metrics.
- Keys: HSM-backed signing and envelope encryption; FIPS 140-2 compliance required.

POC plan / milestones (agreed in email):
- Week 0: NDA + lab access (complete)
- Week 1-2: Deliver hardened deployment checklist + artifacts (Redwood) -> Due 2026-03-18
- Week 3: On-site lab deploy of Private control plane in Aegis lab (air-gapped config)
- Week 4: Performance testing (1k sustained, 2.5k spike) + security scans
- Week 5: Security remediation + final sign-off -> security approves or provides remediation list

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Procurement expects enterprise contract + SOW for Private deployment. Budget conversation started; target ARR band $250k-$1M.
- Competing vendors on shortlist: IBM Watson (legacy SI fit), Verint (contact center incumbents), internal build (in-house runtime). Aegis favors Redwood for inference economics + model fallback features but needs hardened on-prem proof.

Key stakeholders:
- CTO (final tech sign-off)
- SecOps Director (IL5/compliance gating)
- Contact Center Ops lead (use-case owner)
- Procurement (commercial)

Open questions / action items:

- Legal to provide data residency and flow diagrams for air-gapped install (Priya).
- Delivery to produce an install checklist showing zero outbound egress from GPU nodes (Lena).
- Procurement to surface target contract vehicle (GSA-like) or need to go via prime.

Next steps: deliver hardened on-prem checklist by 2026-03-18, then schedule architecture walk on 2026-03-25 (tentative).

- "If we can't have HSM + IL5 controls, won't pass SecOps" (paraphrase).
